newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee extends nuclear power plant outage.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee extends nuclear power plant outage.

text.p: Maine Yankee Atomic Power Co said Monday sorting out problems with electrical cables at the 910 megawatt (MW) facility is taking longer than expected, and it does not expect the work to be finished before mid-March.

The company had earlier estimated the project, which involves ensuring proper separation and inspection of the facility's wiring after several problems were detected, would be would be completed in mid-February.
The Maine Yankee power plant, in Wiscasset, Maine, was shut December 6, to correct the cabling problems.

"More than 120 temporary contractors have been hired to assist with this complex project. Nonetheless, the cable inspection will require more time to complete than originally estimated. Maine Yankee now expects that work to be completed in mid-March," the company said in a statement.
The company said about 40 percent of the cabling review was completed, during which six problems were found that required "corrective action."
The company also said an inspection of the facility's fuel assemblies has shown defects in eight assemblies installed in the plant's 1995 refueling.
The assemblies will be replaced during the current outage, with the work likely finished by mid-February.

The Maine Yankee power plant is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent Bangor Hydro, five percent Maine Public Service Co and 10 percent by other regional utilities.
